text: The present (1925-6) issue of the CHINA YEAR BOOK is again considerably larger than any of its predecessors. The Chapters on “Mines and Minerals,” “Education,” “Products,” “Labour,” “Opium,” “Commerce,” “Shipping,” “Currency,” etc., have been rewritten and brought up to date. The Report of the Shanghai Child Labour Commission is reprinted in full in the Chapter in “Labour.” “The Political Summary” describes events up to the end of March, 1925. The Chapter on “Defence appears at the end of the Book. New Chapters include a Summary of Medical Events.” “Political Parties,” “Taxation” a “Bibliography for 1924,” and a documented Chapter on “China’s Constitutions” and Election Laws.” THE TERMS OF THE GOLD FRANC SETTLEMENT ARE INCLUDED IN AN APPENDIX.

text: With reference to the offer of new shares dated the 10th June, 1925 (made to existing shareholders of the Company) by the terms of which the sum of $30 per share was to be paid on or before the 15th July, 1925, and the sum of $30 per share on or before the 15th October, 1925, the Directors have decided that as regards those shareholders (having a registered address in the Far East) who do not feel themselves (owing to present circumstances) in a position to accept the Company's offer on or before the 15th July, 1925, a further opportunity shall be given to them to take up the new shares.

label: text
text: Such shareholders may accordingly take up the new shares on or before the 15th day of September, before the 15th day of September, 1925, and may pay the first instalment of $30 per new share on or before that date. They will, however, be required to pay interest at 6 per cent. per annum on the amount of such first instalment from the 15th day of July, 1925, until the date of payment.

text: The second instalment of $30 per share will be payable not later than the 15th December, 1925, and interest upon it will be payable from the 16th October, 1925, at the rate of 6 per cent per annum until the date of payment.

label: text
text: Slightly over a hundred servants are now on strike at the British Legation, including some of the clerks as well as domestics.

label: text
text: The students are picketing the North and West gates to prevent servants entering the Legation Quarter and are also intimidating the families of servants living in the Legation Quarter with the object of compelling the latter to quit.

label: text
text: The strike has evidently been planned for a long time, and a considerable sum has been collected for the purpose. All strikers have been paid a month's wages by the students.

label: text
text: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs so far outwardly appears to have done very little to end the strike, but the British Legation is hopeful of an early settlement. Up to the present there is no sign of the strike spreading to the employees of other British residents in Peking.

label: text
text: It is understood that at a meeting of students, this afternoon, it was decided to attempt to induce all Chinese, in foreign employ in Peking, to go on strike.

label: text
text: The number of Legation strikers increased yesterday and the employees of the Legation Electric Power House walked out early this morning, bringing the number of strikers to over 200.

label: text
text: The strikers' committee has passed a resolution, stating that their object is to make the British Charge d'Affaires and the British Government realise their mistaken policy in China and arouse the patriotic sentiments of the Chinese people.

label: text
text: A Bureau has been opened at the National University, where employees of any foreigners in Peking, desirous of striking, may register and receive a month's wages. But, hitherto, practically there has been no response. The Legation officials are still optimistic that a settlement will be reached very shortly.

label: text
text: While the bunking group conducting the liquidation of the Stinnes concern emphatically denies that differences have arisen with the Stinnes family, the Rheinisch Westfaelische Zeitung, the mouthpiece of the family, says that the bunks are unwilling to assume additional obligations on the ground that the fresh liabilities of the concern are continually being discovered.

label: text
text: The paper adds that unless the banks alter their methods the concern will declare bankruptcy or request the Court to supervise the liquidation. It asserts that Herr Schicht, President of the Reichsbank, approves the action of the banks, "thereby surrendering German economic life to ruin." The paper adds that if the concern declares bankruptcy, the banks also will require assistance.

label: text
text: Sir Edwin Stockton, in the "Times," questions the wisdom of holding a judicial enquiry into the recent Shanghai trouble, in view of the time already elapsed.

label: text
text: He thinks there ought to be enough evidence at the Government's disposal to enable it to decide the merits of the occurrence, which started the trouble. An effort should be made to reach an adjustment on information available. He does not imagine the Chinese Government will be reluctant to clear up matters without delay as far as the Shanghai shooting episode is concerned.

text: Seven thousand Freemasons attended the luncheon at Olympia today, in connection with the Masonic Million Memorial Fund Festival.

label: text
text: The Duke of Connaught presided and the Duke of York and Prince Arthur of Connaught were present. The Duke of Connaught announced that subscriptions totalled £826,000 including £417,000 from London lodges alone.

label: text
text: The Oversens lodges came in for special congratulation in the course of the proceedings, the Duke of Contaught referring in the warmest terms to their assistance.

label: text
text: It is semi-officially stated that the Chinese Government will, on August 11, issue invitations to the Powers to participate in a Tariff Conference, to be held at Peking on October 15.

label: text
text: The preparatory commission for the conference, at a meeting yesterday decided that the conference should be convened, on October 15, in Peking.

label: text
text: It is believed that the Cabinet, will shortly agree to this, but no official statement has been issued. It is understood that no invitations will be sent to the Powers till the formal receipt from Washington arrives, confirming the unanimous ratification of the Nine Power Treaties.
